title: Free plan memory limit
body: The Redis Cloud free database refuses writes at about 28 MB of values with an OOM error.

title: Free plan connections
body: The 31st connection to the free database is refused with max number of clients reached.

title: No TLS on the free plan
body: Encryption in transit cannot be turned on for the free database; the REST API refuses enableTls.

title: REST API tasks
body: Every create, update and delete call returns 202 and a task id; errors arrive inside the task.

title: Alerts replace the whole list
body: Sending one alert in a database update switches off every alert left out of the list.

title: Sentinel failover time
body: Sentinel promoted a replica 4.4 seconds after the primary was killed, three of them for down-after-milliseconds.

title: Old primary stays master
body: A restarted former primary answers as master for about eleven seconds until Sentinel reconfigures it.

title: WAIT counts one connection
body: WAIT only waits for the writes sent on the same connection, so a fresh connection returns at once.

title: Cluster failover and node timeout
body: With a 15 second cluster-node-timeout the replica took over after about 19 seconds; with 3 seconds after about 5.

title: CLUSTERDOWN during failover
body: Until a replica takes over, uncovered slots make every node answer CLUSTERDOWN for about a second.

title: Hash tags keep keys together
body: Keys sharing a hash tag in braces land in the same slot, so multi-key commands work on a cluster.

title: Atomic slot migration
body: CLUSTER MIGRATION moved a thousand slots in 44 ms under write load without client errors.

title: LFU keeps hot keys
body: Under allkeys-lfu both frequently read and frequently written keys survived eviction.

title: LRM evicts read-only keys
body: allkeys-lrm protects keys that are rewritten and evicts keys that are only read.

title: Volatile policies need TTLs
body: A volatile eviction policy never removes keys without an expiry; with none, writes are refused.

title: Client-side caching
body: redis-py with RESP3 served a thousand reads from local memory and was told when the key changed.

title: Broadcast tracking
body: In broadcasting mode the server pushes invalidations for every key under a prefix and keeps no per-key table.

title: Claiming stuck stream messages
body: XAUTOCLAIM hands messages from a dead consumer to a live one after a minimum idle time.

title: Idempotent producers
body: XADD with IDMP returns the same entry id for a retried message instead of writing a duplicate.

title: Giving a message back
body: XNACK releases a pending message without acknowledging it so another consumer can claim it at once.

title: Read-only functions on replicas
body: A function registered with no-writes runs on a replica through FCALL_RO; writing functions get READONLY.

title: ACL selectors
body: A selector adds a second, narrower rule set to a user, such as appending only to audit streams.

title: Module commands in ACL categories
body: Since Redis 8, removing the write category also blocks JSON and time series writes.

title: Change data capture from Postgres
body: RDI copied a Postgres table into Redis and kept it in sync, with changes visible within about a second.

title: Kubernetes operator
body: One Helm release created the Redis Enterprise operator and a three-node cluster on kind in about four minutes.

title: Trial licence shard limit
body: The operator's admission webhook refused a database that would exceed four shards on the trial licence.

title: Agent memory for AI agents
body: Agent Memory stores conversations, extracts long-term memories in the background and recalls them per user.

title: Routing user intents
body: Intent Router matches a query to an intent by embedding similarity and returns its target and score.

title: Resumable agent streams
body: Agent Mesh lets a client reconnect to another server and receive the events it missed.

title: Persistence and fsync
body: With appendfsync everysec writes stay fast while at most about a second of data can be lost.
